# Generated test fixtures

Everything in this folder is generated by code in this repository. No recordings, no
third-party audio, no copyrighted lyrics. Licence: GPL-3.0-or-later, like the rest of
the project. Each file must stay under 600 KB.

| File | Made by | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `tiny.jksong` (557,703 bytes) | `make_tiny.py` | A complete `.jksong` v1.0 song: 4.0 s, 44.1 kHz stereo, four 24-bit FLAC stems (`lead_vocal`, `backing_vocals`, `drums`, `other`) generated by `tests/conformance/synth.py` (seed 7), letter-timed lyrics "Hello café" / "naïve world," (precomposed `é`, and `i` + U+0308 combining diaeresis as one grapheme), a 32x32 generated PNG cover, key "A major", 120 BPM, default settings in slot A. |

Properties worth knowing when using `tiny.jksong` in tests:

- The `other` stem peaks above full scale (1.08), so it is stored scaled with
  `gain` = 1.090909 (the SONG_FORMAT 4.2 headroom rule); the other stems have gain 1.0.
- It was written in exact-residual mode (`other` = source minus the decoded other
  stems), so all four stems at unity sum back to the generated source within half an
  LSB of the `other` stem.
- Its settings slots are 16 KiB, not the usual 256 KiB (any multiple of 4096 is valid;
  it halves the file). A test that saves a large `lyrics_override` into it may get
  `SlotPayloadTooLarge` and has to take the full-rewrite path.
- Each stem has a SEEKTABLE with a point every second and a STREAMINFO MD5.

Regenerate (deterministic: same bytes with the same numpy / libsndfile versions;
sha256 `502d5bfe...093d8` with numpy 2.5.5, soundfile 0.14.0, libsndfile 1.2.2):

```bash
source scripts/devenv.sh
"$JK_BUILD/studio-venv/Scripts/python.exe" -I tests/fixtures/generated/make_tiny.py
cargo run -p jk-format --example jksong-verify -- tests/fixtures/generated/tiny.jksong --strict
```

## `demo-song.jksong` (2,483,029 bytes)

The demo song: bundled with the app for the self-check, and the ground truth for the
lyrics-ticker test. It is the one exception to the 600 KB rule above (the work order
allows this fixture up to 3 MB: a 40 s song with four stems cannot be smaller without
losing what it is for).

- Made by `jukeoke-cli make-demo-song` (code: `crates/jk-engine/src/demo.rs`).
  Deterministic: the same bytes every run (2,425,490 bytes, sha256 `069f0e8c...0b061b14d`
  on Windows x86-64 since the app was renamed Open Mic, whose name the manifest records;
  2,425,489 bytes, `d350ad64...3aef9eb37`, under the working name Jukeoke with the 1.1
  writer; `1ddb91d8...9f06e0786` with 1.0 before Work Order 2; sines come from the
  pure-Rust `libm` crate, the noise from an integer PRNG).
- Since 2026-11-20 (Work Order 2) it also carries its melody guide, added by
  `jukeoke-cli guide add` (SONG_FORMAT 1.1 `guide` + `guide.curve`: 42 notes, builder
  `jk-pitch pyin+notes 0.3.0` since 2026-11-24), so the self-check's "Practice guide" item reads a stored
  guide from the bundled copy. Every other chunk and both settings slots are byte-identical
  to the generated song (the guide is added by the raw-copy rewrite of SONG_FORMAT 7.1);
  regenerate with `make-demo-song` and then `guide add` (crates/jk-engine/tests/demo.rs
  checks exactly that). Regenerated 2026-11-20 (Stage 3b) after the 1.1 writer: the earlier
  copy still had the 1.0 manifest; its guide's notes are identical.
  Regenerated again 2026-11-24 (the first CI run on GitHub caught it): the manifest names
  the app, renamed Open Mic on 2026-11-22, and the guide comes from builder 0.3.0
  (2,483,031 bytes with the guide, sha256 `e0173c93...0197e67bc`).
- "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star": words by Jane Taylor (1806), melody the traditional
  French tune; both public domain. All audio is synthesised: a sine-and-harmonics
  "voice" (`lead_vocal`), a quiet harmony a third below in lines 3-6 (`backing_vocals`),
  a soft kick / snare / hat loop (`drums`), a chord pad (`other`).
- 40.0 s (1,764,000 frames), 44.1 kHz, **mono** stems (SONG_FORMAT allows `channels` 1),
  24-bit FLAC carrying 16 significant bits (every sample a multiple of 256, coded as
  FLAC "wasted bits") to keep the file small; all gains 1.0, STREAMINFO MD5 and a seek
  table every second. Key C major, 120 BPM, a 96x96 generated PNG cover.
- Structure: intro 0-2 s, lines 1-4 at 2-18 s, **instrumental break 17.9-26 s** (8 s with
  no singing), lines 5-6 at 26-34 s, outro to 40 s.
- Lyrics: 6 lines, 139 timed graphemes, `source: user_text`, `checked: true`. Every
  syllable is one note (0.5 s, the last of each line 1.0 s), sung over the first 90 % of
  the note. Letter times are exact **by construction**: onset consonants 60 ms each, coda
  consonants 60 ms each, extra vowels of the nucleus 80 ms each, and the first vowel holds
  for the rest of the note (held vowels long); punctuation is a zero-length grapheme at
  the end of its word. `jk_engine::demo::demo_lyrics()` returns the same data.

Regenerate and check:

```bash
source scripts/devenv.sh
cargo run --release -p jk-cli -- make-demo-song tests/fixtures/generated/demo-song.jksong
cargo run --release -p jk-cli -- verify --strict tests/fixtures/generated/demo-song.jksong
```
